patterns.assimilated-prefix: A prefix changes its last letter to match the next sound: ad+com becomes ac+com.
patterns.double-consonant: Two of the same letter, usually where a prefix meets a base.
patterns.single-consonant: Looks like it should double, but does not.
patterns.doubling-1-1-1: One syllable, one short vowel, one final consonant: double before a vowel suffix.
patterns.silent-letter: A letter you cannot hear, usually kept from the older form of the word.
patterns.schwa: An unstressed vowel that sounds like 'uh', so the letter has to be remembered.
patterns.ie-ei: The i/e pair, decided by the root, not by a rhyme.
patterns.soft-c-g: c or g sounding soft because e, i or y follows.
patterns.sh-spelling: The /sh/ sound spelled ci, ti, si or ss.
patterns.suffix-ant-ent: The -ant/-ent choice, set by the Latin verb it came from.
patterns.keep-e: Keep the silent e when adding -ly.
patterns.base-change: The base loses or changes a letter when the suffix goes on.
patterns.greek-marker: Greek loan markers: ph, ch as /k/, y as short i, rh, ps.
patterns.ough: The ough family, one spelling, many sounds.
patterns.homophone-trap: A real word sits next door and sounds the same.
patterns.unique: A one-off. Learn it as itself.

words.why: Two prefixes stack up, so two doubles: ad becomes ac, then com keeps its m.
A companion shares bread with you. Double c from ad, single p from panis.
To accord is to bring hearts together, so cord, with cc from ad.
You bring a thing to a head, to a chief. The i comes before the e.
Ad becomes ag before gress, to step at someone. Then gress keeps its ss.
An amateur does it for love. The -eur ending is French and stays whole.
The /sh/ here is spelled ci, the same trick as in sufficient.
It appears, so ad plus parere gives pp. Latin -ent verbs take -ent.
To appreciate is to set a price on it. Price gives the ci.
Ad becomes at before tach. One t would make a different word.
Avail means to be of worth. Add -able because avail is a whole word.
A sea-trade word for sharing damage costs. The middle e is a lazy 'uh'.
Norse afugr means back to front, plus -ward, direction. Three letters, w-k-w.
The ending is -ain, the same lazy ending as captain and mountain.
Old English crushing plus a French spelling, so ui, and s not z.
Greek word for a public statement. The middle e and the -ory are both schwa.
Greek for a sleeping place. Three e's in a row of syllables, no a anywhere.
Commit doubles its t before -ee. Two m, two t, two e, in that order.
From common. Double m from com plus mun, then a single n.
Same root as common and communicate, so the same double m.
Compete keeps its e even though you cannot hear it. Then -ition.
Hidden inside is science, to know. Knowing with yourself.
Same hidden science as conscience, then -ous for the adjective.
Contra means against, vers means turn. Turned against each other.
Things that come together suit you. Venire gives -ien, then -ence.
Com becomes cor before respond, so two r's meet in the middle.
From critic. The c stays c, and British English takes -ise.
Curious loses its u when it becomes curiosity. Care, not carelessness.
Finis means end, so there is a finite hiding inside. Never an a.
Despair is inside it, hope gone. Sperare gives -per-, never -par-.
You set a limit, a terminus. One r, and -mined like the word mine.
Envelope wraps up, develop unwraps. No e on the end, no double p.
A book of sayings. Dict means say, so dictate and predict are cousins.
Disaster loses its e before -ous. An ill-starred event.
Really Red and Super Shy. Two r, two s, unlike harass.
Environ means around. Keep its n, then add -ment. You cannot hear it.
-ment starts with a consonant, so equip does not double. Compare equipped.
-ed starts with a vowel, so the p doubles. Compare equipment.
Special plus -ly, so two l's. The /sh/ is ci, from species.
Agger is a heap. To exaggerate is to heap it up, so gg.
Excel doubles its l before -ent. Rising above the rest.
To exist is to stand out. Latin -ere verbs take -ence, not -ance.
Explain loses its i here. Making something flat and plain.
Family plus -ar. Known to the household.
From outside. The g was added later by copying reign, so it is silent.
Four keeps its u, forty drops it. English changed its mind in the 1500s.
Frequens means crowded. Latin -ens becomes English -ent.
Govern plus -ment. Keep the n, even though nobody says it.
Guard and guarantee share the gua. The ending is -tee, like referee.
One r, two s. The opposite pattern to embarrass, which has both doubled.
Hinder loses its e before -ance. Say it: hin-drance, two syllables.
Idem means the same. Your identity is what stays the same. No n after i.
In becomes im before m: nothing in the middle, so it happens now.
Keep the e of immediate before -ly. Same rule as definitely and sincerely.
Not divisible: divide is inside it. Then the -ual ending, like usual.
To strike between two things. The ending is -fere, not -fear.
Inter ends in r, rupt starts with r. Break between, so two r's.
Lingua is a tongue. The u after g is silent, the -age is a lazy 'ij'.
Time you are allowed. This one is e before i, unlike achieve.
Lightning drops the e of lighten. Lightening means getting brighter.
British English doubles the l of marvel before -ous. American English does not.
Three syllables, not four. Mischief plus -ous, and no extra i.
A flexing muscle looked like a mouse under the skin. Muscular shows the c.
One collar, two sleeves: one c, two s. Then -ary.
The person who dwells near. Same eigh as eight and weigh.
Something that harms you a little. French ui, then -ance.
Ob becomes oc before c. To seize a space. One p.
Ob becomes oc, then curr means run. One r here, two in occurred.
A wind blowing towards the harbour. Ob becomes op before port.
A place for speaking, from French parler. The hidden i is the giveaway.
Per means thoroughly. Never spell it pur-, and never swade.
Greek gives ph for /f/ and y for short i. Nature, as in the body.
Judging before you know. Judge is inside it, with no d before the j.
A private law, just for you. Lex means law, so -lege, no d.
You profess, you declare. One f, two s, like confess.
Gramma means writing, as in grammar and diagram. British English keeps -mme.
Pronounce has ou, pronunciation does not. The noun lost it in Latin.
A tail of people. One letter doing the work, with four just queueing behind.
To know again. Cogn means know, so the g must be there even if you skip it.
Re plus commend. One c, two m, because the double belongs to commend.
It lifts the point up. Levare also gives lever and elevate.
A place that restores you. Restore plus a French -ant ending.
Rhyme borrowed its rh and y from rhythm, its Greek cousin.
No a, e, i, o or u anywhere. Both y's are doing vowel work.
To make holy. Facere, to make, becomes -fice, as in office.
The keeper of secrets. Secret is whole inside it, then -ary.
The ou here says 'oh', as it also does in boulder and smoulder.
Sign hides its g, signature says it out loud. Same word underneath.
Latin for pure. The ending is -cere, soft c before e.
Sincere keeps its e before -ly. Same rule as immediately.
Paid in solidus coins, so soldier holds the word sold.
Greek ch says /k/, as in chorus, character and echo.
Sub becomes suf before f. The /sh/ is ci, as in ancient.
Sub becomes sug before g. You carry an idea up from underneath.
Greek y for short i. A cymbal is the instrument, a symbol is the sign.
Greek y again, saying short i. Things standing together.
Temper is inside it: a mixing. Say all four syllables to spell it.
Thorough is through with an extra syllable. Same family, same ough.
Twelve turns its v into f, then adds th. Three consonants, all needed.
Vary plus -iety. Four syllables, so say it slowly to hear the e.
Say veg-e-table, four syllables. The hidden e is the one people drop.
Vehere means to carry. The h is silent here but loud in vehicular.
Dutch jachtschip, a hunting ship. English kept the Dutch letters, not the sounds.

off_list.why: Two lots of double s, one in possess and one before -ion.
There is a rat in separate. The middle a is a lazy 'uh', so it has to be remembered.
The prefix in- turns into ir- before an r, so two r's meet.
The /sh/ is spelled ci, the same trick as in ancient and precious.
Know is hiding inside it, silent k and all. Then -ledge, not -lege.
The suffix is -ful, one l, always. Full has two, -ful never does.
Beauty swaps its y for an i before the suffix. The eau is French and stays whole.
Greek gives ch for /k/ and y for short i, the same as in scheme and physics.
